newsitem.title: MEXICO: Zedillo says Mexico health workers to get pay hike.
newsitem.headline: Zedillo says Mexico health workers to get pay hike.

text.p: Mexico's government-paid doctors, nurses and paramedics will receive salary increases as of November that will have an effect of 1.4 billion pesos on the 1997 budget, Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said Wednesday.

"On Nov 1 we will take a step forward in the recovery of salaries for medical doctors, nurses and paramedic workers as I promised you at the start of this administration," Zedillo said in a ceremony marking Day of the Doctor in Mexico.
But Zedillo did not say in his speech how much the pay raises would be in percentage terms.

In addition, he announced the creation of a program to promote productivity and quality in medical services starting in 1997 at a cost of 180 million pesos, plus a 250 million peso program to improve medical services in rural areas.
Zedillo said more than three million Mexicans have basic health care coverage in 380 of the 600 poorest cities in Mexico.
"There are still a lot of Mexicans who live in marginal conditions of health and hygiene, Mexicans who are trapped in an unjust circle of being sick and doing without," Zedillo said.
